name: Memory and Learning
summary: How the brain encodes, stores, and retrieves information across a lifetime.

sections.heading: Types of Memory
sections.content: Sensory memory is an ultra-brief (milliseconds to seconds) trace of raw sensory input. Working memory is the brain's mental workspace (prefrontal cortex), holding roughly four items for seconds to minutes. Long-term memory is potentially permanent storage, divided into explicit (declarative — facts and events) and implicit (procedural — skills and habits) types.

sections.heading: Consolidation and Sleep
sections.content: The hippocampus is critical for converting short-term experiences into long-term memories through consolidation. During sleep (especially slow-wave sleep), the hippocampus 'replays' the day's experiences, strengthening important neural pathways and pruning irrelevant ones. This is why sleep deprivation devastates learning.

sections.heading: Neuroplasticity
sections.content: The brain physically changes with every new experience. Long-term potentiation (LTP) strengthens synaptic connections between frequently co-activated neurons. Over time, repeated practice can increase gray matter density (as seen in London taxi drivers' enlarged hippocampi) or create entirely new neural pathways.
